reasoning: This appraisal uses the direct comparison approach against recent Davidson and same-street sales. Figures are indicative and rely on the comparable evidence overleaf being correct. Grimes Place is a tightly held cul-de-sac of ~15 homes, ~95% owner-occupied.

The anchor is a 4/2 Davidson house on 754 m² that sold $2.30m (Jan 2026) — the most recent, most configuration-similar evidence. The street brackets the subject: a ceiling at 13 Grimes (5/3/2, $2.64m) and 10 Grimes (6/4/3, $2.78m), clearly superior; a floor confirmed by 19 Grimes ($1.85m, Dec 2020, single garage) pre-boom.

Two features pull the subject below the $2.30m anchor: single-car accommodation and likely dated condition. A larger block (~800 m²+) and the premium cul-de-sac position offset this. On balance the subject sits a touch under the anchor unless renovated or holding a city outlook — a most-likely read near $2.2m.
confidence_note: To sharpen: confirm land size & living area (title/contract), internal condition (original vs renovated — the single biggest swing), whether #9 has 1 or 2 car spaces and any district/city view, and pull a CoreLogic 4/2 Davidson sold-comp set <3 months old.
comps_note: Suburb median house price ~$2.40–2.53m to Mar 2026, up ~7% YoY. Sources: Domain (Grimes Place street profile & Davidson sold), First National (4 Grimes), propertyvalue.com.au (19 Grimes), Allhomes. Some land sizes/car counts unconfirmed — verify. Not sales-weighted advice.
